To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the addition of H2O/CH3OH mixtures and Hg2+ ions to the solution of the orthometalated AT215C5 derivative of 9-aminobenzoquinolinium induced a large redshift in the absorption spectrum, which enabled the photometric detection of Hg2+.
we have developed a new colorimetric method for the detection of Hg2+.
the ortho- or para-substitution pattern of aminobenzenesulfonamide-substituted benzoquinolizines with a thiaazacoronand unit determines the type of interaction with Hg2+.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a selective, colorimetric sensor for Hg2+ that operates in aqueous media and that can be applied for the determination of Hg2+.
the design and synthesis of novel metal-ion-selective chromogenic receptors, which are able to detect and discriminate between Hg2+, Mg2+, Ag+, and Pb2+, respectively, in aqueous solutions.
the development of selective colorimetric sensors for Hg2+ based on the 9-ammonio-N-arylbenzo[b] quinolizinium conjugates with AT215C5 in the ortho and para positions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a selective colorimetric detection of Hg2+, Ag+, and Pb2+, as well as Mg2+, is possible with the new chromophores.
Hg2+ is detected in the presence of competing cations in aqueous media and Mg2+ is detected under aprotic conditions.
the Hg(II) ion induces a redshift of the chromophoric absorption band in the presence of the AT215–quinolizium conjugate, while the Mg(II) ion does not induce such a shift.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed two new chromophores, the AT215C–quinolizium and the A15C–quinoliziium derivatives, for selective photometric detection of Hg2+/Ag+ and Mg2+, respectively, in aqueous solution.

the ortho-substituted 9-amino-quinolizinium–crown ethers are selective for Hg2+ over other thiophilic cation, while para-substituted 15-crown-5–9-amino-phenyl-quinolizium conjugate are selective for Mg2+.

the ortho isomers of the crown ether–quinolizium conjugates are suitable for the selective photometric detection of Hg2+, whereas the para isomers are more appropriate for the photometric detection of Mg2+.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ortho substitution pattern of the aminophenyl group of the 9-aminobenzoquinolinium chromophore is crucial for the development of selective and sensitive Hg2+-sensors.
the ortho- and para-substituted AT215C5 and A15C5 derivatives of 9-aminoquinolizinium are useful chromogenic probes for the selective detection of Hg2+, Mg2+, and other cations.
the redshifted absorbance band of the aminocrown ether–quinolizium conjugate is a unique signature of the complexation of the conjugated system by Hg2+ in the presence of competing metal ions.
